P1.evidence: Frame delivered and agreed: 'Really just want to understand where you're at with your fitness journey right now, what's working, what's not, what you're looking to achieve, and then from there, if we can help with that, we can go into all the details about what we've got going on, if that sounds good' — answered 'Yeah, yeah. Cool.' P1a N/A: no setter suffix and no setter notes referenced.

P2.evidence: Four clean hits. Work asked twice and properly — 'What type of work are you doing?' produced the refinery DCS role, and 'What's your working schedule and your family schedule looking like right now?' produced the nine-hour seated day and the pre-work gym slot. Training frequency, session length and the full weight arc all established: 215 down to 180, back to 190-195 across six months. Diet asked directly — 'Did you get back into tracking macros at all, or are you not bothering that anymore?' Height asked. Against that, age was volunteered 23 minutes in and never asked, health conditions were never asked at all, and the only injury screening was a leading statement rather than a question — 'Sounds like you don't have any major injuries or pain or anything like that.' Sleep and energy never came up. The high cholesterol he disclosed as a goal was never followed up in any form.

P3.evidence: The deepest goals work in the batch. The outcome question was asked properly — 'let's say you drop down to 175, 10% body fat, and you got the lean muscle, you're moving better. How do you see your life being different or maybe better?' — and produced cholesterol, self-image and then the real answer: 'I want to be a good role model for my kids because I don't want to grow up telling them, hey, fitness is important, and for them not to see that in my life.' The rep then asked the single best follow-up anywhere in these twelve calls — 'Were your parents like that?' — and got 'No, they were not. And that's why I'm trying to make the change.' That is identity level, reached in two questions. Also good: 'Any particular reason behind 175? Why that one?' What is missing is P3c, and a confirmation reflect — the summary at 00:21:58 states the insight back but never asks 'is that right?'. The larger failure is not in this phase: having reached generational identity at minute 21, none of it was used when the price objection arrived at minute 49.

P4.evidence: Past attempts asked and answered — 'have you ever reached out to somebody to kind of get help with alternative exercises?' produced 'I've never really had any formal training... everything else after that has been empirical, self-taught.' The six-month lapse was traced properly to the house build and confirmed resolved ('is the house still being constructed, or are you done with that now?'). But the structural questions never ran, and on this call they were the whole ballgame: this is a man who took himself from 215 lb to 180 lb self-taught, so the one question that had to be asked is why he needs to pay $6,000 for something he has already done alone. 'The information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?' was never asked in any form, and no gap was ever named. His stated need stayed at 'a little bit more of guidance', which is not worth $6,000 and is precisely why the objection landed on value rather than on affordability.

P5.evidence: Never ran. No two-year question, no willingness-to-settle, no line in the sand. The material was there and unusually clean — genetic high cholesterol, nine hours a day seated, fifteen pounds regained in six months, and children who will learn from what they see him do. The prospect had just said his parents modelled nothing and that is why he is trying to change it; the cost of him repeating that pattern was never put to him.

P6.evidence: P6a ran and ran well, but 25 minutes too late — after the price and after the spouse objection: 'outside of that, do you actually feel like if you went through this, you'd be committed, and it would get you the results that you want?' answered 'I think so. And I can assure you that if I pay $6,000, I will be committed.' Banked before the number, that is a commitment the rep could have held him to. P6b was never asked. P6c is a miss — the price was presented cold at 00:37:10 with nothing secured beforehand, and when hesitation surfaced the rep did not return to Phase 5, which had never run in the first place.

P11.evidence: No close attempted. The prospect deferred to his wife, and the rep never sent the payment link he had described, never offered a deposit, never booked a follow-up and never proposed including the wife on a call. Nothing in the phase was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Clear trigger: 'I would have to consult with my wife... what's mine is ours.' Two moves ran, and both produced useful material. The belief check — 'do you actually feel like if you went through this, you'd be committed?' — got a strong yes. The obstacles question — 'what do you think she might have, let's call them objections to, or concerns about?' — surfaced the guarantee issue, which is exactly what that move exists for. Nothing after that. No 'is there any reason she would not want you healthier and around longer', no separation of genuine joint input from asking permission, and no deposit-with-refund fallback. Worth flagging as a script limitation rather than a rep failure: the scripted line 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' would have been actively counterproductive here, because they share a bank account and had literally just finished building a house together. No follow-up call was offered with the wife on it, which is the obvious missing action.

'It is a significant investment' and 'the price really would be the only thing leaning towards not doing it.' The rep opened with the correct diagnostic and the best-phrased one in the batch — 'the price isn't like seeing the value of investing 6k, or is it more like 6k is a lot and you just don't have that much available?' — which cleanly separated value from capacity and established it was value. Then the play stopped. No HOW-not-SHOULD reframe, no financial picture, no plan structured, and financing was never mentioned despite existing. A direct question about paying up front was answered with a credit-card deflection.

The remote-versus-in-person value objection, which has no scripted play: 'it sounds a little steep by the fact that it's only a person kind of talking to you over the phone and not necessarily there with you.' The rep improvised competently — frame-by-frame video review catching what a live eye misses, daily access versus two or three sessions a week, qualifications, structure, and teaching to fish. The prospect softened ('I completely agree... just because it's different doesn't mean that it's not effective') but the rep never asked whether that resolved the price concern and never returned to the number. This is a third distinct gap in the script alongside the clinical-fit and cheaper-substitute gaps already documented.

Certainty was asked for explicitly, via the wife: 'how much of a guarantee would Trevor provide when it comes to results.' The opening OE move is written for this — 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?' — and none of the play ran. Instead the rep answered with a numeric guarantee, which converts a psychological objection into a contractual claim and is logged as a flag.
No think-about-it stall; the deferral was specifically to his wife.
Timing was in the programme's favour — the house is finished and he is deliberately swinging back to fitness.

notes: The rep reached generational identity by minute 21 — 'Were your parents like that?' is the best question in this batch — and then let it sit unused while the call was decided on price at minute 49. Two concrete coaching actions. First, run P4f: this prospect took himself from 215 to 180 self-taught, and until someone establishes why that is not repeatable, $6,000 has no gap to fill and the objection will always be value. Second, when a prospect asks what the guarantee is, that is an OE trigger, not a request for figures — answering it with '10% body fat and 20 pounds on the lifts' hands an unwritten promise to a man who is about to repeat it to his wife.
